title: perf-delta-scrub-shop-notes-2026-12-02
content:
Perf delta scrub — shop notes (2026-12-02)
Owners: Alicia (lead), Ravi, Maya, Noah, Sofia
Context / Why we met
- Quick sync after yesterday's smoke-wave run showed a ~12% p95 regression for the 4k mixed-seq workload vs baseline (2026-11-28 golden).
- Regression surfaced only on M60-64 (8xA100-ish) pools and was absent on smaller instance shapes.
- Goal: triage possible causes, run small targeted experiments, leave with an action list and owners.

Summary of observed signals
- Bench run summary (from smoke-wave-2026-12-01):
  - qps target: 1.2k stable
  - model: rwkv-30B-quant-v2
  - batch strategy: continuous batching v3, idle_timeout 12ms, max_batch 64
  - p50: +1% vs baseline, p95: +12%, p99: +20%, tail spikes aligned to occasional 200–400ms pauses per node
  - CPU steal and host-level IO noise: small spikes concurrent with tail events (see heatmap_2026-12-01).
- KV-cache hit ratio: unchanged overall but observed increased variance per-worker (std dev up 3x).
- Kernel rollout state: kernel v5 (new matmul tiling tweak) rolled to 30% on M60-64 last night (PR 1287).
- Trace capture: sampled traces show queue depth spikes followed by a long service time on first token after spike; subsequent tokens are normal.

Hypotheses discussed (ranked quick):
1) Kernel v5 tiling change interacts poorly with large-batch hot paths on M60-64 -> causes micro-pauses when certain tiling edge-case hits. (high)
2) Autoscaler/GC interaction: scheduler preemption/GC on node triggers short stalls, amplified at high qps. (medium)
3) Batching heuristic regression: continuous batching now sometimes forms a batch with a heavy-first-request (long prompt) causing head-of-line blocking. (medium)
4) NVMe host background IO spikes causing scheduler jank (low)

Immediate experiments to run (next 24–48h)
A. Kernel rollback canary (owner: Ravi)
   - Roll back nodes in a shadow pool to kernel v4; run the same smoke-wave profile overnight with 20% traffic shadowing.
   - Metrics to compare: p95/p99, per-worker kv-cache variance, trace-first-token latency.
   - Jira: INFRA-3421.

B. Batch composition probe (owner: Maya)
   - Add instrumentation to log batch size distribution + first-request-length histogram in bench harness for 1 hour runs at peak load.
   - Add a pin in harness to force max_batch=32 vs 64 to see sensitivity.
   - Quick check: if p95 drops with max_batch=32, batch head-of-line hypothesis gains weight.

C. Node-level jitter capture (owner: Noah)
   - Run a host-probe daemon on suspect nodes capturing cpu/mem/io/interrupt timestamps at 10ms granularity for 4h window.
   - Correlate with bench trace IDs. If IO/interrupt spikes align to service-time pauses, escalate to infra.

D. Warmup/prefetch tweak (owner: Sofia)
   - Experiment enabling proactive KV-cache prefetch for long prompts to avoid first-token penalty (lightweight toggle in runtime).
   - Run A/B with 5% and 20% of traffic.

Discussion notes / rationale
- Kernel v5 rollout timing matches regression arrival; rolling back is fastest test to isolate code-path issue. Ravi to coordinate with release-engineering for partial rollback.
- We saw similar first-token pauses historically when KVCACHE misses coincided with very large batch assembly (2019-08-ish ticket referenced in confluence). Not identical but worth instrumenting.
- Autoscaler logs didn't show mass evictions, but we need higher-res host telemetry to rule out scheduler jitter.

Acceptance criteria for closing the incident
- Identify primary cause or eliminate top hypotheses.
- If kernel rollback reduces p95 by >=8% vs current -> mark kernel v5 as suspect and open a regression PR/rollback plan.
- If batch composition change reduces p95 by >=5% -> follow-up PR to adjust batching heuristics + tests.

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Ravi: orchestrate kernel-v4 canary on shadow pool, start by 2026-12-03 02:00 UTC, report by 2026-12-03 EOD.
- Maya: add batch/first-length hist logging to harness and run with max_batch=32 and 64, start 2026-12-03 04:00 UTC, initial data by 2026-12-03 14:00 UTC.
- Noah: deploy host-probe to suspect nodes, capture 4 hours, correlate and post findings, by 2026-12-04 10:00 UTC.
- Sofia: flip kv-prefetch toggle in a canary and monitor errors/latency, start 2026-12-03 06:00 UTC, results by 2026-12-04.
- Alicia: maintain slack thread, update Confluence with interim notes, and prepare retrospective doc if we close the loop.

Open questions / to think about
- If this is kernel path dependent, how many other shapes were rolled to v5? Should we halt rollout? (Ops decision after Ravi's canary.)
- Is there a way to get deterministic repro locally? We discussed building a microbench that constructs the exact batch composition to trigger the pause. Maya to try.
- Do we need to increase trace sampling temporarily (x2) to get better signal? Trade-off: cost vs signal.

Follow-ups / next sync
- Quick async updates in #perf-ops. Round-up call scheduled 2026-12-04 09:00 UTC to decide rollback/roll-forward.

Notes to self (Alicia)
- Keep run artifacts: smoke-wave-2026-12-01.{prom,trace,heatmap}. Put them in confluence/perf-lab-index-2026 attachments.
- If kernel is culprit, ask release-eng to add a guard in rollout to exclude M60-64 for now.

End of notes.


(Informal scribbles below — left verbatim)
- saw a trace where worker A had 320ms first-token then rest < 10ms -> suspect initial matmul path fallback.
- check PR 1287 comments: they called out a micro-tile branch for sequences > 2048; could interact with tiling and cuda mem alignment.
- remind: keep shadow runs at 10–20% not to disturb production SLA.
